item.title: Follow cursor pages in listItems
item.brief: Implement the client member of the shared cursor pagination contract. listItems(transport) must return all items in order, following next_cursor until null or absent; the first request sends no cursor and subsequent cursors are passed back unchanged. Update README and ensure npm test passes. Commit the change.

item.title: Implement GET /items cursor pagination
item.brief: Implement the API member of the shared cursor pagination contract for GET /items. Validate optional limit as an integer 1..100, default 20, and validate cursors; malformed inputs return status 400 with {"error":"..."}. Preserve ordering by id; return {"items":[...],"next_cursor":string|null}, with null on the last page. Update README and ensure python3 -m unittest passes. Commit the change.

state.summary:
Implemented GET /items cursor pagination with limit validation (default 20, range 1–100), ordered pages, opaque cursors, and 400 errors for malformed limits/cursors. Updated README and added pagination and validation tests. `python3 -m unittest` passes (6 tests), `git diff --check` passes. Initial whole-change review found oversized digit-string handling; fixed and committed, then delta review passed. Final head b1fca2df0fc275a92334702e6f1e9af7969a5207; no known gaps.

evidence.caption: Baseline and final unit test results

pr.body: Implemented URL-safe base64 cursors representing the last item ID, stable ID ordering, 20-item default and 1–100 limit validation, and HTTP 400 error bodies for invalid pagination parameters. Updated README.md and expanded test_api.py, including full traversal and a 5000-digit limit regression case. Checks: `python3 -m unittest` passed (6 tests); `git diff --check` passed. Initial review's oversized integer conversion finding was fixed in a separate commit and passed delta re-review. Assumption: a cursor must be canonical URL-safe base64 for an ID present in the in-memory catalog.
pr.summary: Added cursor pagination to GET /items. Before: the endpoint returned the full catalog in one response; now: callers can fetch ordered pages with a validated limit and continue using next_cursor.
